issues.legal_issue: Acquisition of land for an integrated public infrastructure project implemented with private-sector participation can be for a public purpose even when a private company benefits from the project.
material_facts: The State adopted a policy to develop an integrated business, tourism and infrastructure project intended to promote the State’s economic and social development.
A state-owned corporation acted as the project’s nodal agency, and the project was to be implemented through a joint venture with a private company.
The project was presented as generating employment, revenues and wider economic opportunities, and the state-owned corporation was to pay the compensation for the acquired land.
issues.conclusion: The acquisition served a public purpose; private-sector participation and benefit to the private company did not make the acquisition invalid.
issues.legal_principle: The inclusive definition of “public purpose” in Section 3(f), read with Sections 4 and 6 of the Land Acquisition Act, 1894, is broad and can encompass a project that benefits the public even if private interests also benefit. Public ownership or direct public use of every part of a project is not essential. The Court relied, among other authorities, on Somawanti v. State of Punjab, State of Karnataka v. Ranganatha Reddy, Pratibha Nema v. State of Madhya Pradesh, State of Karnataka v. All India Manufacturers Organisation, Berman v. Parker and Kelo v. City of New London.

rule.if: land_acquisition_challenge and state_instrumentality_leads_project and project_serves_wider_public_interests and private_sector_participates

predicates.land_acquisition_challenge: A party challenges the compulsory acquisition of land.
predicates.state_instrumentality_leads_project: A government instrumentality leads or coordinates the project for which the land is acquired.
predicates.project_serves_wider_public_interests: The project is intended to produce benefits for the public beyond the interests of a particular private party.
predicates.private_sector_participates: A private company participates in or benefits from implementation of the project.

issues.definition: When a party challenges an acquisition led by a government instrumentality for a project serving wider public interests, private-sector participation does not prevent the acquisition from serving a public purpose.

issues.legal_issue: An integrated and indivisible infrastructure project must be assessed as a whole when deciding whether its land acquisition serves a public purpose.
material_facts: The proposed development combined multiple infrastructure, business and tourism components into one integrated project.
The State and its instrumentality presented the project as structurally and financially integrated and as advancing broader economic and social benefits.
The land acquisition was undertaken to enable development of the integrated project.
issues.conclusion: The project had to be evaluated as a whole rather than by separately testing whether each component served the public interest.
issues.legal_principle: For an integrated and indivisible project, the public-purpose inquiry considers the project in its entirety and its overall public benefits, rather than separating its components. The Court applied this approach alongside the principles governing public purpose under Section 3(f) and acquisition under Sections 4 and 6 of the Land Acquisition Act, 1894, and relied on the integrated-project reasoning in State of Karnataka v. All India Manufacturers Organisation.

predicates.land_acquisition_challenge: A party challenges the compulsory acquisition of land for a project.
predicates.project_is_integrated_and_indivisible: The project combines components that are planned and implemented as one integrated undertaking.
predicates.project_as_a_whole_advances_public_inter: The project, considered in its entirety, advances broader public interests.

issues.definition: If the challenged acquisition is for an integrated and indivisible project whose overall undertaking advances public interests, the public-purpose assessment is made for the project as a whole.

issues.legal_issue: The Part II acquisition procedure applies to land acquired for a public purpose when compensation is paid wholly or partly from public funds, even if a private company participates in the project.
material_facts: The state-owned corporation was the nodal agency for the project and was to pay the entire compensation for the acquired land.
A private company participated in implementing the project through a joint venture with the state-owned corporation.
The acquisition was undertaken for the State’s public infrastructure project, rather than as an acquisition funded entirely by a private company for that company alone.
issues.conclusion: The acquisition could proceed under Part II; the procedure for acquisition for a company under Part VII was not required.
issues.legal_principle: Sections 4 and 6 permit acquisition for a public purpose or for a company. Under the second proviso to Section 6, compensation for a public-purpose acquisition must be paid wholly or partly from public revenues or an applicable public fund; Explanation 2 treats compensation paid from a corporation owned or controlled by the State as paid from public revenues. Part VII, including Sections 39 to 41, applies where land is acquired for a company and the cost is borne entirely by that company. The Court relied on Pandit Jhandulal v. State of Punjab, R.L. Arora v. State of Uttar Pradesh, Pratibha Nema v. State of Madhya Pradesh and Devinder Singh v. State of Punjab.

predicates.land_acquisition_proceeding: The proceeding concerns compulsory acquisition of land.
predicates.acquisition_is_for_public_purpose: The land is acquired for a purpose serving the public rather than solely for a private company’s benefit.
predicates.compensation_is_paid_wholly_or_partly_fr: The compensation is paid wholly or partly from public revenues or by a government-owned or government-controlled corporation.

issues.definition: In a land-acquisition proceeding, when the acquisition is for a public purpose and compensation is paid wholly or partly from public funds, the Part II procedure applies.

issues.legal_issue: Judicial review of the government’s determination that an acquisition serves a public purpose is limited, but the determination may be set aside for mala fides, collateral purpose, absence of any public purpose, illegality, irrationality, unreasonableness or fraud on the statute.
material_facts: The State formed the view that the acquisition was needed for an integrated infrastructure project implemented through its instrumentality.
The compensation was to be paid by the state-owned project agency, and the Court found that the project served broader public interests.
The Court found no basis on the facts to conclude that the acquisition was mala fide, for a collateral purpose, outside the law, irrational or unreasonable, or a fraud on the statute.
issues.conclusion: The government’s public-purpose determination was not to be displaced, and the acquisition proceedings were not invalid on the grounds raised.
issues.legal_principle: The government is ordinarily the primary judge of public purpose, but it is not the sole judge and its determination remains judicially reviewable on recognised grounds. Section 6(3) makes the declaration conclusive evidence of public purpose, but does not protect a colourable exercise of power or fraud on the statute. The Court relied on Hamabai Framjee Petit v. Secretary of State, State of Bombay v. R.S. Nanji, Somawanti v. State of Punjab, Srinivasa Cooperative House Building Society Ltd. v. Madam Gurumurthy Sastry and Bajirao T. Kote v. State of Maharashtra.

rule.if: land_acquisition_challenge and government_determines_public_purpose and not (mala_fide_or_collateral_purpose or no_public_purpose or action_outside_law or irrational_or_unreasonable_action or fraud_on_statute)

predicates.land_acquisition_challenge: A party challenges compulsory acquisition of land on the ground that it does not serve a public purpose or is otherwise unlawful.
predicates.government_determines_public_purpose: The government has determined that the acquisition serves a public purpose.
predicates.mala_fide_or_collateral_purpose: The acquisition was undertaken in bad faith or for a purpose collateral to the stated public purpose.
predicates.no_public_purpose: The acquisition serves no public purpose at all.
predicates.action_outside_law: The acquisition action is outside the authority conferred by law.
predicates.irrational_or_unreasonable_action: The government’s action is irrational or otherwise unreasonable.
predicates.fraud_on_statute: The government used its statutory power to achieve an improper purpose in fraud of the statute.

issues.definition: When the government determines that an acquisition serves a public purpose and none of the listed grounds for invalidating that determination is present, the determination is not set aside.
